original_question: What is a complete characterization of C6-free bricks, where C6 denotes the triangular prism and a brick is C6-free when that graph is not a conformal minor? Equivalently, which bricks are not C6-based under the paper's conformal-minor framework?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s official target. It correctly focuses on bricks, it uses the paper’s conformal-minor notion of freeness, and it correctly identifies the equivalent 'not J-based' language. It also targets the same problem the authors isolate after reducing the broader matching-covered-graph question to bricks.
missing_details: The paper’s graph is \overline{C_6}, the triangular prism (the complement of the 6-cycle); writing C_6 without the bar is potentially misleading, since C_6 ordinarily denotes the 6-cycle.
To make the question stand-alone, 'brick' should be defined: a brick is a connected nonbipartite matching covered graph with no nontrivial tight cuts.
To make the question stand-alone, 'matching covered' should be unpacked: every edge lies in some perfect matching.
To make the question stand-alone, 'tight cut' should be specified: a cut C of a matching covered graph G is tight if |C \cap M| = 1 for every perfect matching M of G.
The conformal-minor condition should be stated explicitly: \overline{C_6} is a conformal minor of G if some bisubdivision H of \overline{C_6} is a subgraph of G and G - V(H) has a perfect matching.
If you use the equivalent 'based/free' phrasing, it should be tied to the paper’s definition: for fixed J, a matching covered graph G is J-based if J is a conformal minor of G, and J-free otherwise.

The nearest official formulation in the published paper is an open problem, stated as Unsolved Problem 1.34; the paper gives partial results and an equivalence with the solid-brick problem for simple nonplanar bricks, but it does not replace the problem statement with that reformulation.
refined_question: Characterize all bricks G—that is, all connected nonbipartite graphs of order at least two in which every edge belongs to some perfect matching and which have no nontrivial tight cuts, where a cut C is tight if |C \cap M| = 1 for every perfect matching M of G—for which the triangular prism \overline{C_6} is not a conformal minor; equivalently, for which there is no bisubdivision H of \overline{C_6} contained in G such that G - V(H) has a perfect matching.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, characterize the bricks that are not \overline{C_6}-based.
justification: This is the exact open problem isolated in the paper after the authors define conformal minors and J-based/J-free graphs and reduce the broader question to bricks. In the published PDF, the target statement is Unsolved Problem 1.34, 'Characterize C6-free bricks,' where the notation refers to the triangular prism \overline{C_6}. The surrounding discussion supplies the needed definitions of brick, conformal minor, and J-based/J-free, records the planar simple case, and later proves that for simple nonplanar bricks the \overline{C_6}-free problem is equivalent to the solid-brick problem up to the Petersen-graph exception. So your draft is essentially on target; the main paper-faithful correction is the notation \overline{C_6} and the explicit unpacking of the conformal-minor framework.
